strategy.audience: Capital allocators and DeFi traders managing multiple concurrent credit positions across fragmented venues.
strategy.problem_statement: Traditional risk containment relies on isolated pools that fragment capital, forcing collateral to sit idle or serve only one job at a time across disconnected silos just to prevent contagion.
strategy.angle: A deterministic 1.1x health factor floor safely enables unified margin accounts, eliminating the need for fragmented pools so the same collateral posted once can support multiple positions simultaneously without systemic contagion risk.

briefs.problem_statement: Traditional risk containment relies on isolated pools that fragment capital, forcing collateral to sit idle or serve only one job at a time across disconnected silos just to prevent contagion.
briefs.angle: A deterministic 1.1x health factor floor safely enables unified margin accounts, eliminating the need for fragmented pools so the same collateral posted once can support multiple positions simultaneously without systemic contagion risk.
briefs.audience: Capital allocators and DeFi traders managing multiple concurrent credit positions across fragmented venues.
briefs.strongest_objection: A unified account sharing collateral across multiple positions at a tight 1.1x health factor floor exposes the borrower's entire collateral pool to liquidation if a single position degrades, whereas isolated pools quarantine losses to an individual position.

briefs.problem_statement: In traditional leveraged credit, cascading liquidations occur because accounts operate without an adequate safety cushion, allowing bad debt to accumulate and spread insolvency across the venue when positions plunge past parity.
briefs.angle: Leverage is easy, but surviving adverse moves is the true challenge. By enforcing an explicit 1.1x health factor floor before underwater insolvency occurs, paired with floor division rounding that prevents protocol-favoring arithmetic distortion, the failure mode of bad debt is arrested before it can threaten solvency or trigger systemic contagion.
briefs.audience: DeFi credit participants, risk managers, and institutional allocators seeking protection against cascade liquidations and bad debt contagion.
briefs.strongest_objection: A strict 1.1x health factor floor forces early liquidations and restricts capital efficiency, potentially closing positions that would have recovered during short-term volatility.

briefs.problem_statement: Autonomous agents currently have payment capabilities to spend capital they hold, but cannot safely access borrowing or leverage because unconstrained autonomous debt risks cascading liquidations and protocol contagion.
briefs.angle: Enabling agents to borrow safely requires hard protocol guardrails; by establishing a strict 1.1x health factor floor and policy-bounded risk management, autonomous agents can take on credit positions without threatening solvency or spilling risk into other accounts.
briefs.audience: Developers building autonomous agent systems and algorithmic trading frameworks seeking automated credit rails.
briefs.strongest_objection: A strict 1.1x health factor floor may trigger liquidations too early during rapid market volatility, wiping out an autonomous agent's strategy and deterring builders from using credit rails over self-funded spot operations.

ruling.reason: capital_efficiency directly addresses the core tension in the topic between isolated pools and unified margin accounts. It grounds its argument in EV-59eca1bff3bb and EV-96734d01c8c5 without hallucinating metrics, and provides a clear, honest self-objection acknowledging that unified accounts expose cross-position collateral to liquidation compared to strict pool isolation.
